paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְיוֹסֵ֔ף הִנֵּ֥ה אָבִ֖יךָ חֹלֶ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׁנֵ֤י בָנָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְאֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass after these things, that one said to Yosef, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Menasheh and Ephraim.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter opens with the cycle's first deployment of the death-approach predicate *choleh* ('sick'). The ASV-baseline 'sick' is preserved; the lexeme is uncontested. The opening also re-introduces both Yosef-sons by name in the order *Menasheh ve-Ephraim* (the elder before the younger, per birth-order), an ordering that the chapter will deliberately reverse by v 5 (*Ephraim u-Menasheh*) and again by v 20 (*Ephraim lifnei Menasheh*). The chapter's signature literary-architectural move — the firstborn-priority reversal — is already signalled by the birth-order naming here at v 1 versus the inverted naming at vv 5 and 20, even before the hand-crossing at v 14 makes the reversal physical. Sarna *JPS Genesis* (1989) p. 324; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* (1986) p. 184; Alter *Five Books of Moses* (2004) p. 283 note the naming-order pattern as part of the chapter's deliberate setup.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה בִּנְךָ֥ יוֹסֵ֖ף בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַזֵּק֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הַמִּטָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And one told Ya'aqov, and said, Behold, thy son Yosef cometh unto thee: and Yisra'el strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.

paragraphs.commentary: Three convergent flags. *Va-yitchazzeq Yisra'el* — the Hithpael of *chazaq* deploying the deathbed-self-rallying-strength idiom, cross-corpus 1 Kgs 2:2 (David's *ve-chazaqta ve-hayita le-ish* to Shelomoh) and the broader patriarchal-and-royal deathbed-strength tradition (overlay `va-yitchazzeq-yisrael-deathbed-self-rallying-strength-gen48`). The name-shift Ya'aqov (v 1 narration / v 2a *va-yagged le-Ya'aqov*) → Yisra'el (v 2b action) continues the Yosef-cycle's marked alternation (overlay `yaaqov-yisrael-name-shift-cycle-wide-pattern-gen48`, sibling-extension of the cycle-wide pattern across Gen 45 → 46 → 48). And *ha-mittah* — the chapter's narrative-action of *sitting up on the bed* materially reinforces the MT bed-reading against the LXX/Heb 11:21 *ha-matteh* ('staff') variant treated at Gen 47:31 (overlay `mt-lxx-mittah-mateh-bed-vs-staff-textual-variant-gen47`). The v 2 narrative-action — Yisra'el *sitting* on the *mittah* — is itself an internal textual-witness for the MT vocalization.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֥ל שַׁדַּ֛י נִרְאָֽה־אֵלַ֥י בְּל֖וּז בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיְבָ֖רֶךְ אֹתִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov said unto Yosef, El Shaddai appeared unto me at Luz in the land of Kena'an, and blessed me,

paragraphs.commentary: The covenant-memory recital opens by naming the *El Shaddai* theophany at Luz. The patriarchal divine-name compound *El Shaddai* (central `el-shaddai`) recurs at Gen 17:1, 28:3, 35:11, 43:14, and here at 48:3 — the six P-or-P-adjacent patriarchal occurrences. The toponym *Luz / Beit-El* (central `bethel-luz-name-etymology`) is the place of two prior theophanies in the Ya'aqov cycle (Gen 28 the ladder; Gen 35 the *El Shaddai* renaming). Ya'aqov's recital here conflates: Gen 35:9-12 explicitly names *El Shaddai* at the Luz renaming; Gen 28:13 names YHWH at the ladder; Gen 17:1 anchors the *El Shaddai* compound for the entire patriarchal line. The recital's unified-theophanic-thread — multiple appearances treated as a single divine-encounter-tradition — culminates at v 16 in the *ha-mal'akh ha-go'el* compression. Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 325; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 184-185; Cassuto *Genesis* II on the patriarchal-blessing-recital tradition.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הִנְנִ֤י מַפְרְךָ֙ וְהִרְבִּיתִ֔ךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ לִקְהַ֣ל עַמִּ֑ים וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י אֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: and said unto me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a company of peoples, and will give this land to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.

paragraphs.commentary: The covenant-memory recital cites the Gen 35:11 *El Shaddai* theophany's three-fold formula. (a) *Hineni mafrekha ve-hirbitikha* — the Hiphil-causative variation on the Gen 1:28 *peru u-rvu* imperative (central `peru-urvu`, appliesTo extended to v 4); Westermann documents the Gen 1 / 35 / 47 / 48 / Exod 1 *peru-urvu* / *parah-rabah* multiplication-thread as the P-source's structural marker. (b) *Qhal ammim* 'a company of peoples' — the patriarchal-promise-formula (new central `qhal-ammim-congregation-of-peoples-patriarchal-promise-formula`); cross-corpus Gen 28:3 (Yitzchaq's blessing of Ya'aqov, with the Yosef-direction reversal); Gen 35:11 (the immediate Beit-El precedent *goy u-qhal goyim*); cross-corpus Deut 23 and Ezek 38 for the broader *qhal*-distribution. (c) *Achuzzat olam* 'an everlasting possession' — the patriarchal land-promise institutional formula (central `achuzzah`, appliesTo extended to v 4, with the *achuzzat olam* sub-formula linking Gen 17:8 to Lev 25:34 documented in the entry). The three sub-formulae together form one of the cycle's tightest patriarchal-promise compressions.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה שְׁנֵֽי־בָנֶיךָ֩ הַנּוֹלָדִ֨ים לְךָ֜ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד־בֹּאִ֥י אֵלֶ֛יךָ מִצְרַ֖יְמָה לִי־הֵ֑ם אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּרְאוּבֵ֥ן וְשִׁמְע֖וֹן יִֽהְיוּ־לִֽי׃

i18n.en: And now thy two sons, who were born unto thee in the land of Mitsrayim before I came unto thee into Mitsrayim, are mine; Ephraim and Menasheh, even as Re'uven and Shim'on, shall be mine.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's institutional centerpiece. *Li-hem* + *yihyu li* (compressed: 'they are mine; they shall be mine') is the corpus's clearest single-verse formal-adoption formula (new central `adoption-formula-li-yihyu-ephraim-menasheh-as-reuven-shimon`). The act effects three institutional consequences. First, Ephraim and Menasheh become tribal-eponyms in their own right — the twelve tribes are now Yosef's two sons functioning as full tribal heads in place of Yosef-as-one-tribe. Second, the *bekhor* double-portion is silently redirected: Yosef receives two tribal allocations rather than one, the institutional content of *bekhorah* (central `bekhorah-birthright-firstborn-status`). Third, the comparison *ki-Re'uven ve-Shim'on* anchors the equivalence to the actual firstborn (Re'uven) and second-born (Shim'on) of Ya'aqov, making the elevation institutionally exact rather than honorific. Cross-corpus 1 Chr 5:1-2 makes the connection explicit: *u-vne Re'uven bekhor Yisra'el... u-v-challelo yetzu'ei aviv nittenah bekhorato livnei Yosef ben-Yisra'el* ('the sons of Reuven the firstborn of Yisra'el, but because he defiled his father's couch, his birthright was given to the sons of Yosef ben-Yisra'el'). Num 26 (the wilderness census) lists Menasheh and Ephraim as separate half-tribes, confirming the adoption's institutional effect in the legal-census record. The note that the inverted naming *Ephraim u-Menasheh* (younger before elder) appears here for the first time anticipates vv 13-20. Named scholarship: Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 326; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 186-187; Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* pp. 631-633; Alter *Five Books of Moses* p. 284; Levenson *The Death and Resurrection of the Beloved Son* (1993) on the displaced-firstborn motif. NO Christian-supersessionist 'adoption-of-the-Gentiles' typology is asserted; the institutional reading is sufficient and is mainstream named scholarship.

paragraphs.text: וּמוֹלַדְתְּךָ֛ אֲשֶׁר־הוֹלַ֥דְתָּ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם לְךָ֣ יִהְי֑וּ עַ֣ל שֵׁ֧ם אֲחֵיהֶ֛ם יִקָּרְא֖וּ בְּנַחֲלָתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And thy issue, that thou begettest after them, shall be thine; they shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.

paragraphs.commentary: The adoption's corollary-clause. Only Ephraim and Menasheh become tribes (governed by the v 5 adoption-formula central). Any subsequent Yosef-sons — if there are any (the corpus does not record any; the qualification is hypothetical-or-precautionary) — would remain administratively subsumed under the Ephraim-and-Menasheh territorial allotments rather than constituting separate tribal eponyms. *Al shem acheihem yiqqar'u be-nachalatam* ('they shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance') is the institutional-precision clause: future-Yosefide descendants take their inheritance-portion through the Ephraim or Menasheh nachalah, not as independent tribal recipients. The two verses together (v 5 + v 6) define the adoption's exact scope; the entry's appliesTo covers both.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲנִ֣י ׀ בְּבֹאִ֣י מִפַּדָּ֗ן מֵ֩תָה֩ עָלַ֨י רָחֵ֜ל בְּאֶ֤רֶץ כְּנַ֙עַן֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ בְּע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־אֶ֖רֶץ לָבֹ֣א אֶפְרָ֑תָה וָאֶקְבְּרֶ֤הָ שָּׁם֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔ת הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: And as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Kena'an in the way, when there was still some distance to come unto Efrat: and I buried her there in the way to Efrat (the same is Beit-Lechem).

paragraphs.commentary: The Rachel-grief-recall mid-blessing — one of the chapter's most-cited literary observations (overlay `rachel-grief-recall-mid-blessing-gen48`). Ya'aqov interrupts the legal-adoption act to recall Rachel's death and burial. Sarna, Westermann, Alter, and Brueggemann read the interruption as motivational: the adoption that elevates Rachel's two grandsons (via Yosef) into full tribal status compensates Rachel's premature death and her two-sons line not multiplying into more tribes. Two lexical sites: *kivrat eretz* 'some distance' (overlay `kivrat-eretz-rare-idiom-gen48`) is a rare idiom whose force is debated — the only other HB occurrence is 2 Kgs 5:19. The Efrat / Beit-Lechem identification (overlay `efrat-beit-lechem-toponym-davidic-cross-corpus-gen48`) is a cross-corpus toponym anchor: Mic 5:1 (the Beit-Lechem-Efratah birth-of-the-ruler prophecy); 1 Sam 17:12 (David's father Yishai 'an Ephrathite of Beit-Lechem'); Ruth 1:2 + 4:11 (the Naomi-Elimelekh-Boaz Ephrathite genealogy). The triple of lexical flags is handled as three overlay entries rather than one consolidated 'Rachel-burial-tradition' entry; the Davidic-reception is the load-bearing cross-corpus reach and is overlay-housed pending a future cross-corpus promotion-candidate.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥רְא יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי־אֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el beheld Yosef's sons, and said, Who are these?

paragraphs.commentary: The narrative pivot from legal-adoption (vv 5-7) to the blessing-ritual (vv 8-20) opens with Yisra'el's apparent inability to recognize Yosef's sons. The cycle-wide name-shift continues here with Yisra'el at the seeing-and-asking moment (overlay extended). Sarna and Alter note the narrative-tension: Yisra'el's *mi-eleh* ('who are these?') at v 8 is followed by v 10's explicit blindness-notice — Yisra'el can see something (he 'beholds' the boys) but cannot recognize them. The question reads as a quasi-formal-prelude to the blessing (the patriarch asks who is presented before pronouncing the blessing), echoing the Gen 27:18 *mi-atah beni* ('who art thou, my son?') of Yitzchaq's blindness-deception scene. Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 188-189; Hamilton pp. 634-635; the Gen 27 ↔ Gen 48 deliberate-mirror is governed by the v 10 entries.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־אָבִ֔יו בָּנַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־לִ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים בָּזֶ֑ה וַיֹּאמַ֕ר קָֽחֶם־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַאֲבָרֲכֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his father, They are my sons, whom the Elohim hath given me here. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef's identification deploys *ba-zeh* ('here'), a deictic-locative naming Mitsrayim as the place where Elohim 'gave' him the sons — a quiet Mitsri-context marker for the adoption-act. The cohortative-blessing introduction *qachem-na elai va-avarakhem* ('bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them') echoes the patriarchal-blessing-protocol of Gen 27:7, 25-27 (Yitzchaq's instructions to Esav/Ya'aqov). The Gen 27 mirror is structurally pervasive at v 10 (see commentary there); here at v 9 the parallel-protocol — *na* particle, *avarakhem* cohortative — is the first verbal echo.

paragraphs.text: וְעֵינֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כָּבְד֣וּ מִזֹּ֔קֶן לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְא֑וֹת וַיַּגֵּ֤שׁ אֹתָם֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק לָהֶ֖ם וַיְחַבֵּ֥ק לָהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Now the eyes of Yisra'el were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's most-cited literary observation: the deliberate Gen 27 blindness-echo. Gen 27:1 reads *va-tikheina einav me-r'ot* ('his eyes were dim from seeing') — the deception-mechanism that enabled Ya'aqov's theft of Esav's blessing. Gen 48:10 reads *ve-einei Yisra'el kavedu mi-zoqen lo yukhal lir'ot* — the same structural-clause with the verb *kaved* ('be heavy') substituting for *kahah* ('be dim'). The lemma differs; the narrative-trigger function is identical and the editorial direction is inverted: Yitzchaq was deceived; Ya'aqov here knowingly crosses his hands (the inversion is explicit at vv 14, 17-19 *sikkel et-yadav* + *yada'ti veni yada'ti*). The central `kahah-eynayim-patriarchal-blindness-narrative-trigger` is extended to GEN-WOH-48:10 with rationale-extension documenting the *kaved* / *kahah* lexical-shift and the inversion-of-deception; a sibling overlay `kavedu-einav-mi-zoqen-gen27-gen48-blindness-echo` is wired bidirectionally to mark the chapter-specific literary-echo and the named scholarship (Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 327; Alter *Five Books of Moses* pp. 285-286; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* pp. 238-241; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 188-189; Brueggemann *Genesis* on the inversion-of-deception). The name-shift Yisra'el continues.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף רְאֹ֥ה פָנֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א פִלָּ֑לְתִּי וְהִנֵּ֨ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֹתִ֛י אֱלֹהִ֖ים גַּ֥ם אֶת־זַרְעֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el said unto Yosef, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, the Elohim hath let me see thy seed also.

paragraphs.commentary: *Re'oh fanekha lo fillalti* — the verb *pilel* (Piel) here in the rare sense 'to think / expect / hope' (overlay `pilel-expect-hope-rare-sense-gen48`). The standard Piel of *palal* is 'to pray, intercede, mediate' (the Hannah-tradition, the Mosheh-intercession-tradition, etc.); the 'expect / hope' sense is hapax-or-near-hapax. ASV-baseline 'I had not thought' captures the Hebrew without forcing into the standard 'pray / intercede' register. Cross-corpus comparison: Ps 106:30 *va-ya'amod Pinchas va-yefallel* ('Pinchas stood up and executed judgment' — another non-prayer Piel deployment, also debated). The *gam et-zar'ekha* ('also thy seed') emphatic-doubling deploys *gam* as the surprise-amplifier — Yisra'el did not expect to see Yosef's face; he sees *also* the seed. Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* pp. 635-636; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 189-190; HALOT s.v. *palal* Piel.

paragraphs.text: וַיּוֹצֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֹתָ֖ם מֵעִ֣ם בִּרְכָּ֑יו וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ לְאַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef brought them out from between his knees; and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.

paragraphs.commentary: Two flags. First, the Yosef-cycle dream-and-fulfilment-arc obeisance-keyword recurs (central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`, appliesTo extended to GEN-WOH-48:12): Yosef bows with his face to the earth before his father, in the cycle's continuing pattern of dream-fulfilment that began at Gen 37:7-10 and ran through Gen 42:6, 43:26-28, 44:14, 47:31. The v 12 occurrence is a marked-inverted-direction instance: here Yosef bows before Ya'aqov rather than the brothers bowing before Yosef, completing the cycle's bow-pattern from both directions. Second, *me-im birkav* 'from between his knees' (overlay `bein-birkav-adoption-on-the-knees-ritual-gen48`) flags the adoption-on-the-knees ritual: the boys had been *between Ya'aqov's knees* (the patriarchal adoption-position; cross-corpus Gen 50:23 *al-birkei Yosef* — Yosef's great-grandchildren *born upon his knees*). The bein-birkav / al-birkei knees-as-adoption-locus is one of the corpus's recognized adoption-rituals (Speiser *AB Genesis* p. 358; Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 328; Brichto *The Names of God* p. 199; ANE comparative-evidence from Nuzi and Hittite-law). The Gen 50:23 occurrence will be wired bidirectionally as a sibling-pair to this entry when Gen 50 is processed.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח יוֹסֵף֮ אֶת־שְׁנֵיהֶם֒ אֶת־אֶפְרַ֤יִם בִּֽימִינוֹ֙ מִשְּׂמֹ֣אל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בִשְׂמֹאל֖וֹ מִימִ֣ין יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּגֵּ֖שׁ אֵלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Yosef took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Yisra'el's left hand, and Menasheh in his left hand toward Yisra'el's right hand, and brought them near unto him.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef's careful positioning: Ephraim (the younger) in Yosef's right hand toward Ya'aqov's left; Menasheh (the elder) in Yosef's left hand toward Ya'aqov's right. The arrangement honors the *yad-yemin* ('right hand') priority: the *bekhor* (firstborn, Menasheh) is positioned to receive the right-handed paternal blessing. Yosef's choreography assumes Ya'aqov will follow the standard right-hand-on-elder protocol. The central `firstborn-priority-reversal-irony` is already applied to v 13 (per its appliesTo); the entry's rationale covers the Gen 48 hand-crossing as the corpus's most-deliberate firstborn-reversal instance. The name-shift Yisra'el continues.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־יְמִינ֜וֹ וַיָּ֨שֶׁת עַל־רֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וְה֣וּא הַצָּעִ֔יר וְאֶת־שְׂמֹאל֖וֹ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה שִׂכֵּל֙ אֶת־יָדָ֔יו כִּ֥י מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim's head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Menasheh's head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Menasheh was the first-born.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's iconic moment. Ya'aqov *stretches* his right hand to Ephraim's head (the younger) and his left to Menasheh's head (the elder) — *sikkel et-yadav* ('guiding his hands wittingly' ASV; new central `sikkel-et-yadav-hand-crossing-piel-philological-crux`). The Piel of *sakhal* sits at a philological crux. The verb's *sakhal*-root carries a semantic-range covering both 'to act with insight / understanding / wisdom' (the cognitive register; cf. *maskil* 'wise / prudent', *sekhel* 'insight') AND 'to lay crosswise / to cross over' (the spatial register, perhaps developed from a separate root or as a denominative). Three named-scholarship reading-camps. (a) **Cognitive**: Sarna, von Rad, Alter read *sikkel* as 'he acted with deliberate-wisdom regarding his hands' — the verb names the knowingness of the act, with the hand-crossing implied by context. (b) **Spatial**: Speiser, Westermann, Hamilton, Wenham read *sikkel* as 'he crossed his hands' — the verb names the spatial-act, with the deliberation implied by *ve-hu ha-tza'ir* ('and he was the younger') + *ki Menasheh ha-bekhor* ('for Menasheh was the firstborn'). (c) **Both**: the Piel-intensive captures both senses at once — the *knowing-act* IS the hand-crossing; the verb-form's polyvalence is editorially-deliberate. The ASV's 'guiding his hands wittingly' captures the cognitive sense; modern translations (NJPS 'crossing his hands'; NRSV 'crossing his hands') prefer the spatial sense. The central entry documents the philological crux without adjudicating. *Bekhorah* (central) extends to v 14 (the *ha-bekhor* clause makes the institutional-stake explicit).

paragraphs.text: וַיְבָ֥רֶךְ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ הִתְהַלְּכ֨וּ אֲבֹתַ֤י לְפָנָיו֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֔ק הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ הָרֹעֶ֣ה אֹתִ֔י מֵעוֹדִ֖י עַד־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he blessed Yosef, and said, The Elohim before whom my fathers Avraham and Yitzchaq did walk, the Elohim who hath fed me all my life long unto this day,

paragraphs.commentary: The blessing-formula opens with two parallel divine-name-clauses, both with the definite-article *ha-Elohim*. The first names the deity-of-the-patriarchal-walking: *asher hithallekhu avotai lefanav Avraham ve-Yitzchaq* (new central `hithallekh-lefanai-patriarchal-walking-before-elohim-covenantal-formula`). The Hithpael of *halakh* + *lefanai* names the patriarchal habitual life-conduct in the divine-presence; cross-corpus saturation Gen 5:22 + 24 (Chanokh), Gen 6:9 (Noach), Gen 17:1 (Avraham), Gen 24:40 (Avraham retrospective), 1 Sam 2:30 + 35 (the priestly-house), 1 Kgs 2:4 + 3:6 + 8:23 + 8:25 + 9:4 (the Davidic-conduct formula), 2 Kgs 20:3 / Isa 38:3 (Chizqiyah), Ps 56:14 + 116:9 (worshipper-in-the-land-of-the-living). The existing central `tamim-walk-before-god-covenant` covers the Gen 17:1 *hithallekh lefanai veheyeh tamim* paired-imperative; the present central covers the broader patriarchal-walking-before-Elohim covenantal-formula across its non-Gen-17 deployments. The second clause names the deity-as-shepherd: *ha-Elohim ha-ro'eh oti me-odi ad ha-yom ha-zeh* (new central `elohim-ha-ro-eh-divine-shepherd-metaphor`). The participle *ro'eh* ('shepherding / feeding') is one of the corpus's most-load-bearing divine-metaphors; cross-corpus Ps 23:1 (*YHWH ro'i*), Ps 80:2 (*ro'eh Yisra'el*), Isa 40:11 (*ke-ro'eh edro yir'eh*), Ezek 34 (the shepherd-of-Israel chapter), Mic 7:14, Jer 23. The ASV 'fed' (KJV likewise) preserves the participial-feeding sense; modern translations prefer 'shepherded' (NJPS, NRSV, Alter). The *me-odi ad ha-yom ha-zeh* deploys the formula treated at Gen 47:26 (central `ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`); the v 15 use is autobiographical-individual rather than editorial-aetiological, and the central's appliesTo is extended to GEN-WOH-48:15 with rationale-extension noting the register-difference (Childs JBL 1963 documents both registers).

paragraphs.text: הַמַּלְאָךְ֩ הַגֹּאֵ֨ל אֹתִ֜י מִכָּל־רָ֗ע יְבָרֵךְ֮ אֶת־הַנְּעָרִים֒ וְיִקָּרֵ֤א בָהֶם֙ שְׁמִ֔י וְשֵׁ֥ם אֲבֹתַ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם וְיִצְחָ֑ק וְיִדְגּ֥וּ לָרֹ֖ב בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: the messenger who hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Avraham and Yitzchaq; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's theological signature. *Ha-mal'akh ha-go'el oti mi-kol-ra* — 'the messenger who hath redeemed me from all evil' — is grammatically the *third* term of the v 15-16 blessing-formula's divine-naming series: *ha-Elohim* (v 15a, the deity-of-the-patriarchal-walking) + *ha-Elohim* (v 15b, the deity-as-shepherd) + *ha-mal'akh* (v 16a, the redeeming-messenger). The three are joined by a single optative-verb *yvarekh* ('bless'): the construction names them as a unified-grammatical-subject. The compression is editorially-deliberate (new central `ha-mal-akh-ha-go-el-mi-kol-ra-unified-theophanic-redeemer-formula`). The *mal'akh* / *Elohim* identification is one of the corpus's most-debated theological-architectural data — the messenger who is and is not Elohim. The Ya'aqov-cycle's theophanic-thread compresses Gen 28:13-15 (YHWH at the ladder), Gen 31:11-13 (the *mal'akh ha-Elohim* in the dream identifies himself as *ha-El Beit-El*), Gen 32:25-30 (the wrestling-stranger blesses Ya'aqov and is identified as having seen 'Elohim face to face'), Gen 35:9-15 (El Shaddai at Luz). The *go'el* 'redeemer / kinsman-redeemer' vocabulary is cross-corpus Job 19:25 (*go'ali chai*), Isa 49:7+26, Isa 60:16, Ruth 4 (the legal *go'el* institution). Named scholarship: A. Rofé *Mal'akhei Elohim* (1979) on the *mal'akh* texts; G. von Rad *Genesis* OTL pp. 412-413 on the proto-monotheistic 'compromise' reading; W. Brueggemann *Genesis* (Interpretation) pp. 369-370 on the personalist-relational divine-name; N. Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 329 on the conflation; J. Hamilton *NICOT Genesis 18-50* pp. 638-639; B. Childs *The Book of Exodus* on the *go'el* kinsman-language; J. Levenson on the Genesis-cycle's theophanic-thread; C. Westermann *Genesis 37-50* pp. 190-191 on the *mal'akh*-and-El identification; M. Smith *The Origins of Biblical Monotheism* on the broader West-Semitic *mal'akh* tradition. STRICT lens-discipline maintained throughout the central rationale: NO Christian 'Angel of the Lord' / Christophany / Trinitarian-typology pre-resolution is offered; NO WoH-distinctive *mal'akh*-as-'messenger-from-a-designer-civilization' synthesis is advanced. Two further lexical flags: *yidgu la-rov* ('let them grow into a multitude' — overlay `yidgu-la-rov-multiply-like-fish-hapax-sense-gen48`) deploys a denominative-verb from *dag* 'fish' in the unique sense 'multiply like fish'; the verb is hapax-or-near-hapax with this nuance and is one of the corpus's most-distinctive prolific-multiplication images. *Ve-yiqqare bahem shemi ve-shem avotai* ('let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers' — overlay `yiqqare-bahem-shemi-patriarchal-name-bequest-formula-gen48`) is the patriarchal-name-bequest formula; cross-corpus Num 6:27 (the priestly blessing's *ve-samu et-shemi al-bnei Yisra'el*), Jer 14:9 (*shemekha aleinu niqra*), Isa 4:1, Deut 28:10.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּי־יָשִׁ֨ית אָבִ֧יו יַד־יְמִינ֛וֹ עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וַיֵּ֣רַע בְּעֵינָ֑יו וַיִּתְמֹ֣ךְ יַד־אָבִ֗יו לְהָסִ֥יר אֹתָ֛הּ מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשׁ־אֶפְרַ֖יִם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And when Yosef saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Menasheh's head.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef's intervention. *Va-yera be-einav* — 'and it was evil in his eyes / it displeased him' (overlay `va-yera-be-einav-displeasure-idiom-gen48`) — is the standard displeasure-idiom; cross-corpus Gen 21:11 (Avraham re Sarah's request to send Hagar away), 38:10 (YHWH re Onan), 2 Sam 11:25 + 27 (David's adultery), 1 Kgs 11:6 (Shelomoh). *Va-yitmokh yad-aviv* — 'and he held up / supported his father's hand' (overlay `va-yitmokh-uphold-support-yosef-gesture-gen48`) — deploys *tamakh* in the physical-grasping sense; cross-corpus Ps 17:5 (the worshipper's steps), 41:13 (the integrity-upheld), Prov 4:4. The ASV's 'held up' captures the upward-supporting gesture (Yosef trying to lift Ya'aqov's right hand from Ephraim to redirect it to Menasheh); NJPS 'took hold of' captures the grasping. The central `firstborn-priority-reversal-irony` is already applied here.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶל־אָבִ֖יו לֹא־כֵ֣ן אָבִ֑י כִּי־זֶ֣ה הַבְּכֹ֔ר שִׂ֥ים יְמִינְךָ֖ עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto his father, Not so, my father; for this is the first-born; put thy right hand upon his head.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef's verbal correction: *lo-khen avi ki-zeh ha-bekhor* ('not so, my father; for this is the firstborn'). The deictic *zeh* ('this one') + the bekhor-claim makes Yosef's protest institutionally-precise: Menasheh is the *bekhor* by birth, and the right-handed blessing belongs to the *bekhor*. The central `bekhorah-birthright-firstborn-status` extends to v 18 (the institutional-stake explicit). The verse sets up Ya'aqov's refusal-and-articulation at v 19.

paragraphs.text: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן אָבִ֗יו וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יָדַ֤עְתִּֽי בְנִי֙ יָדַ֔עְתִּי גַּם־ה֥וּא יִֽהְיֶה־לְּעָ֖ם וְגַם־ה֣וּא יִגְדָּ֑ל וְאוּלָ֗ם אָחִ֤יו הַקָּטֹן֙ יִגְדַּ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ וְזַרְע֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֥ה מְלֹֽא־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

i18n.en: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: howbeit his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's explicit articulation of the firstborn-reversal pattern. *Yada'ti veni yada'ti* ('I know it, my son, I know it' — emphatic doubling) makes the act knowing and deliberate. The Gen 27 inversion is now complete: where Yitzchaq blessed in blindness-and-deception, Ya'aqov blesses in dim-eyed-but-explicit knowledge. The principle is articulated: *achiv ha-qaton yigdal mimmenu* ('his younger brother shall be greater than he'). The central `firstborn-priority-reversal-irony` already covers this verse; its existing rationale documents the Gen 25:23 → 27 → 29 → 48 → David/Shelomoh arc as the corpus's structural-axiom of younger-displaces-elder election. The rationale is extended in this pass to mark the v 19 occurrence as the pattern's *explicit articulation locus* — the only verse in the cycle where the patriarch verbally states the principle. Two further flags. *Va-yma'en aviv* — 'and his father refused' — deploys the Piel of *me'en* (overlay `me-en-refusal-verb-yosef-cycle-echo-gen48`); cross-corpus Gen 37:35 (Ya'aqov's *va-yma'en le-hitnachem*, his refusal to be comforted at Yosef's loss), Gen 39:8 (Yosef's *va-yma'en* refusal of Potifar's wife). The chapter-internal echo is editorially-marked: Ya'aqov refuses Yosef as he himself once refused all comfort over Yosef. *Melo ha-goyim* — 'fullness of nations' (overlay `melo-ha-goyim-fullness-of-nations-rom-11-reception-gen48`) — is one of the corpus's most-cited Pauline-reception phrases; Rom 11:25 cites *to plērōma tōn ethnōn* ('the fullness of the Gentiles') in the eschatological framework of Israel-and-the-nations. The overlay documents the Rom 11:25 reception as named-scholarship-observation only; NO Christian-theological adjudication is offered on the supersession or fullness questions. The translation surface remains ASV-baseline 'a multitude of nations'. NO theological-Christian replacement-typology is pre-resolved; the v 19 articulation is treated as the corpus's election-principle articulation, mainstream named scholarship: von Rad on patriarchal election-theology; Brueggemann; J. Levenson *The Death and Resurrection of the Beloved Son* (1993) on the displaced-firstborn motif; Greenspahn *When Brothers Dwell Together* (1994) on the systemic-pattern.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבָ֨רֲכֵ֜ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֮ לֵאמוֹר֒ בְּךָ֗ יְבָרֵ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְשִֽׂמְךָ֣ אֱלֹהִ֔ים כְּאֶפְרַ֖יִם וְכִמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־אֶפְרַ֖יִם לִפְנֵ֥י מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee will Yisra'el bless, saying, the Elohim make thee as Ephraim and as Menasheh: and he set Ephraim before Menasheh.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's liturgical legacy. *Yesimkha Elohim ke-Ephrayim ve-khi-Menasheh* — 'the Elohim make thee as Ephraim and as Menasheh' — is the ONLY blessing-formula from Genesis that becomes a fixed liturgical formula across post-biblical Jewish tradition (new central `yesimkha-elohim-ke-ephrayim-liturgical-blessing-formula`). The *Birkat ha-Banim* tradition — the Friday-night father-to-son blessing recited in Jewish households across millennia — quotes this verse verbatim for sons. (For daughters the parallel tradition uses *Yesimekh Elohim ke-Sarah Rivkah Rachel ve-Le'ah* — the four matriarchs.) Named scholarship: Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 330; Heinemann *Prayer in the Talmud* (1977) on the liturgical-reception; Reif *Judaism and Hebrew Prayer* (1993); the post-biblical reception tradition documented across the rabbinic-and-liturgical scholarship. The note that Ephraim comes first in the formula (per vv 14, 17-19) makes the liturgical-blessing itself an embodiment of the firstborn-reversal: Jewish parents bless their sons by invoking the YOUNGER-elevated-to-firstborn name first. Plus *bekha yvarekh Yisra'el lemor* — 'in thee will Yisra'el bless, saying' (overlay `bekha-yvarekh-yisrael-by-thee-shall-bless-formula-gen48`) — the patriarchal-name-in-the-blessing-formula pattern; cross-corpus Gen 12:3 (*ve-nivrekhu bekha kol mishpechot ha-adamah*), Ruth 4:11-12 (*yitten YHWH et-ha-ishah ha-ba'ah el-beitekha ke-Rachel u-khe-Le'ah*) — the Boaz-and-Ruth wedding-blessing in the same liturgical-formula structure. *Va-yasem et-Ephrayim lifnei Menasheh* ('and he set Ephraim before Menasheh') is the chapter's final formal-act of the reversal; the central `firstborn-priority-reversal-irony` covers this verse. NO theological-supersession reading is pre-resolved; NO WoH spin on the liturgical-formula. The translation surface remains ASV-baseline.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף הִנֵּ֥ה אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת וְהָיָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם וְהֵשִׁ֣יב אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ אֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el said unto Yosef, Behold, I die: but the Elohim will be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's Exodus-return-promise echo. *Ve-hayah Elohim immakhem ve-heshiv etkhem el-eretz avoteikhem* — 'and the Elohim will be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers' — echoes the Gen 46:4 compound formula *anokhi ered immekha Mitzraymah ve-anokhi a'alkha gam-aloh* (central `anokhi-immekha-divine-presence-and-descent-promise-formula`, appliesTo extended to GEN-WOH-48:21). The v 21 deployment is the cycle's *partial-fulfilment-promise* in deathbed-context: Ya'aqov is dying in Mitsrayim, but the deity *Elohim immakhem* ('with you') will execute the *heshiv* ('bring back') component to fulfil the descent-and-return covenantal-structure announced at Gen 46:4 and at Gen 28:15. The Exodus-narrative will fulfil the promise. *Hinneh anokhi met* — 'behold, I die' (overlay `hinneh-anokhi-met-deathbed-self-announcement-formula-gen48`) — is the patriarchal deathbed-self-announcement formula; cross-corpus Gen 50:5 (Yosef's recall of this), Gen 50:24 (Yosef's own *anokhi met* deathbed announcement). The trio Gen 48:21 → 50:5 → 50:24 forms the cycle's deathbed-self-announcement arc. The name-shift Yisra'el continues.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲנִ֞י נָתַ֧תִּֽי לְךָ֛ שְׁכֶ֥ם אַחַ֖ד עַל־אַחֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָקַ֙חְתִּי֙ מִיַּ֣ד הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחַרְבִּ֖י וּבְקַשְׁתִּֽי׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Emori with my sword and with my bow.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's parting formal-act and one of Genesis's most-cited cruxes (new central `shekhem-achad-polysemy-historical-redactional-crux`). Two convergent issues. (a) **The *shekhem* polysemy.** The noun *shekhem* covers (i) 'shoulder' (the lexical-baseline; cross-corpus Job 31:36, Isa 9:5), (ii) 'a portion / a share' (the metonymic extension; the *shekhem achad* idiom 'one portion'), (iii) the proper-name *Shekhem* (the city, cross-corpus Gen 12:6, 33:18-20, 34, 35:4, 37:12-17, Josh 17:7, 20:7, 21:21, 24:1+32, Judg 9, 1 Kgs 12). The v 22 *shekhem achad* admits all three readings: 'one portion above thy brethren' (ASV-baseline lexical reading) versus 'Shechem alone above thy brethren' (proper-name pun, anticipating Josh 24:32 where Yosef's bones are buried *be-Shekhem*). The pun is one of the corpus's most-cited; Speiser, Sarna, Cassuto, Hamilton, Skinner, Westermann all discuss it. (b) **The historical-redactional crux.** *Asher laqachti mi-yad ha-Emori be-charbi u-ve-qashti* — 'which I took from the hand of the Emori with my sword and with my bow.' Ya'aqov claims to have *taken* (Shekhem? a portion?) from the Emori by force of arms. But in the Genesis narrative Ya'aqov did NOT take Shekhem; Shim'on and Levi did, by stratagem, in Gen 34 — and Ya'aqov disavowed the act at Gen 34:30 and again at Gen 49:5-7 (the deathbed-curse). Three named-scholarship reading-positions. (i) **Source-critical fragmentary** (Skinner, Speiser): the verse preserves a fragment of an alternative tradition (E or fragmentary J) in which Ya'aqov did conquer Shekhem; the Gen 34 narrative reflects a different source. (ii) **Harmonizing** (Cassuto, Hamilton, Wenham): the verse refers to a non-Gen 34 incident now lost, or to Gen 34 with Ya'aqov claiming as patriarch what his sons did under his (de facto) authority. (iii) **Irreducibly difficult** (Westermann): the verse is a textual-and-narrative crux that the modern critical tradition has not solved. The central documents the three reading-camps without adjudicating; STRICT lens-discipline: NO WoH ANE-conquest synthesis; NO theological adjudication; the *shekhem* polysemy and the historical-redactional crux are documented as named-scholarship-observation only. The ASV-baseline 'one portion' is preserved on the surface (per the lexical-reading consensus), without precluding the Shekhem-pun reading.
